rs-01-c1.text: The Rust Team (2015). Announcing Rust 1.0. Rust Blog.
rs-01-c1.quote: Today we are very proud to announce the 1.0 release of Rust

rs-01-c1.text: Steve Klabnik and Carol Nichols (2024). What Is Ownership? (The Rust Programming Language). doc.rust-lang.org.
rs-01-c1.quote: When the owner goes out of scope, the value will be dropped.
rs-01-c1.claim: Every value has exactly one owner, a variable. When the owner goes out of scope, the value is dropped

rs-01-c1.text: Steve Klabnik and Carol Nichols (2024). What Is Ownership? (The Rust Programming Language). doc.rust-lang.org.
rs-01-c1.quote: To ensure memory safety, after the line `let s2 = s1;`, Rust considers `s1` as no longer valid.
rs-01-c1.claim: so s2 owns the string and s1 is no longer usable

rs-01-c2.text: Steve Klabnik and Carol Nichols (2024). References and Borrowing (The Rust Programming Language). doc.rust-lang.org.
rs-01-c2.quote: At any given time, you can have either one mutable reference or any number of immutable references.
rs-01-c2.claim: Mutable references (&mut T) allow exactly one writer and no readers.

rs-01-c3.text: Steve Klabnik and Carol Nichols (2024). Rc<T>, the Reference Counted Smart Pointer (The Rust Programming Language). doc.rust-lang.org.
rs-01-c3.quote: Note that `Rc<T>` is only for use in single-threaded scenarios.
rs-01-c3.claim: Rc<T> gives shared ownership through single-threaded reference counting
